free_tier.stated: $150 in free credits for every new Temporal Cloud account, expiring after 90 days; a credit card is required to sign up
free_tier.notes: After the credits are used or 90 days pass, usage is billed with no base monthly fee at $50 per million Actions on pay-as-you-go, plus storage. The open-source Temporal server is free software that the user installs and runs on a rented or free machine.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated on the pages read

retention.stated: closed workflow histories kept for a configurable retention period, up to 90 days on Temporal Cloud
retention.notes: Longer retention uses the Export feature.

egress.terms: not applicable: workers poll Temporal Cloud; no traffic allowance is published

interface_detail: the Cloud Ops API is a public HTTP API and a gRPC API at saas-api.tmprl.cloud:443, authenticated by an API key; tcld and the temporal CLI cloud extension manage namespaces, users and keys. The vocabulary has no gRPC term.
tooling: the Temporal SDKs (Go, Java, Python, TypeScript, .NET, Ruby, PHP), tcld and the temporal CLI. As a last resort the open-source server, which the user installs and runs on a rented or free machine.
chaining: A card-gated 90-day credit; for durable execution with no card, the hosted Inngest free tier comes first.

limits.value: closed workflow histories retained up to 90 days

limits_note: On-Demand capacity starts at 500 Actions per second and auto-scales on 7-day usage.
binding_note: The credit expires after 90 days, and a card is taken at sign-up.

identity_cost.detail: A credit card is required to sign up for Temporal Cloud; the sign-up page offers a work email or Google or Microsoft sign-in, and AWS or GCP marketplace routes. The card is not charged during the first 90 days while credits remain.

reliability_note: After the credits run out or 90 days pass, usage is billed to the card on file.
confidence_note: Credits, card requirement, retention and interfaces are read on first-party pages; nothing behind the sign-up was read.
